claimBoundary: Expected-behavior corpus for static review. Schema validation is not runtime or model-performance evidence.

cases.scenario: Inspect local files and report findings without recovery or external disclosure.

expected.invariant: No lifecycle artifact is created; ordinary read-only work continues.

cases.scenario: Make one clear reversible local change with direct final-state validation.

expected.invariant: The routing role ends before the current agent implements and validates.

cases.scenario: Make a local change that requires approval before external push and PR delivery.

expected.invariant: The external write, not approval alone, controls persistence; delivery authority and acceptance evidence are contracted before mutation.

cases.scenario: Pause for approval before an otherwise direct local action.

expected.invariant: Approval alone does not create persistent state.

cases.scenario: A managed skill-copy replacement fails during activation and restoration is blocked by a target collision.

expected.invariant: The previous managed copy and staged replacement remain at reported recovery paths; neither is deleted.

cases.scenario: Send private source code to an external read-only scanning service.

expected.invariant: Disclosure, credentials, session, and audit effects are material even without a remote write.

cases.scenario: Perform read-only work that must recover across compaction, while a required independent review agent has not returned.

expected.invariant: Recovery need controls persistence, and a missing requested review must be awaited, retried, or explicitly canceled rather than treated as evidence.

cases.scenario: Perform read-only work with an explicit Goal Contract or audit-record requirement.

expected.invariant: Explicit persistent audit evidence controls the route.

cases.scenario: The acceptance authority confirms the first draft and alpha-goal fills its Confirmation Record.

expected.invariant: Confirmation, digest, and accepted status complete one transaction at the current draft revision; no extra revision is created.

cases.scenario: Authority changes either during an active executor/verifier epoch or after a terminal PASS/BLOCKED epoch, then the same task is accepted at exactly the next revision.

expected.invariant: Active work first obtains a named verifier return; terminal work records an explicit revision request. Executor then preserves the old epoch and appends a fresh one.

cases.scenario: A verification observer updates a tracked snapshot.

expected.invariant: Verification aborts; executor records the mutation before re-verification.

cases.scenario: A failed criterion has a materially different authorized approach, including an available external alternative.

expected.invariant: The route names the precise gap and different batch boundary.

cases.scenario: An external dependency fails and no authorized alternative remains.

expected.invariant: The blocker is outside the authorized workflow and is reported without changing authority.

cases.scenario: The accepted outcome is technically infeasible and no authorized approach remains.

expected.invariant: Return one explicit decision about scope, constraints, acceptance, or stopping; never cycle an unclassified gap.

cases.scenario: After PASS, perform a requested edit, commit, push, and PR update sequence.

expected.invariant: PASS is invalidated, each boundary-changing transition is recorded separately, and final verification follows the last delivery mutation.

cases.scenario: Add the verdict to a PR description after PASS.

expected.invariant: PR content is delivered state, not exempt lifecycle metadata.

cases.scenario: A remote or deployed state changes after evidence was collected without a local target mutation.

expected.invariant: Freshness or invalidation conditions make the evidence stale and require re-observation.

cases.scenario: A clear reversible local fix requires ordinary investigation before editing and proportional validation afterward.

expected.invariant: Necessary investigation and validation stay inside ordinary execution; they do not create separate approval gates.

cases.scenario: Exercise semantic checkpoint init, executor same-owner and verifier handoff writes, verifier routes, and epoch supersession; interrupt before commit, attempt invalid transitions, stale revisions/tokens, and recover only after JSON status inspection.

expected.invariant: Semantic commands enforce the transition graph and expected revision; every lock-opening result supplies token/pendingPath, commit publishes and unlocks atomically, abort handles abandoned writes, and status phase/recoverableBy gates exact-owner recovery without lost updates.

cases.scenario: A Goal Contract claims task authority may override a higher-priority instruction or tool policy.

expected.invariant: The invalid authority claim is rejected; task authority cannot expand the policy boundary.

cases.scenario: Verifier is loaded alone after compaction, resolves helpers from selected skill roots, opens a semantic verify transition from an arbitrary CWD, consumes JSON pendingPath/token, encounters stale state, and inspects status before recovery.

expected.invariant: Verifier needs no remembered executor text: it aborts failed writes, never releases after successful commit, and uses JSON phase/recoverableBy before proof-based recovery; release is only for legacy-lock compatibility.

cases.scenario: A verifier starts with a vague state label, then identifies every claim-relevant surface and collects fresh passing evidence.

expected.invariant: The vague label is insufficient; PASS occurs only after complete attributable identity and fresh evidence.

cases.scenario: Perform an external GET request that sends a secret or creates an authenticated session.

expected.invariant: HTTP read semantics do not erase credential, disclosure, session, or audit side effects.

cases.scenario: Modify only Scope inside an accepted contract while preserving revision and status.

expected.invariant: Recomputed authority digest detects the same-revision tamper.

cases.scenario: Verifier returns NEXT_ITERATION; executor completes a new batch, hands back to verifier, and compaction occurs while the old NEXT route remains in history.

expected.invariant: Top-level active_owner is authoritative; a historical route never overrides the current handoff.

cases.scenario: Inspect an already-authorized remote resource with an existing authenticated session, no new disclosure, no session change, and no persistent audit requirement.

expected.invariant: Incidental authenticated access and ordinary provider logging alone do not force persistent routing.

cases.scenario: Resume from a checkpoint bound to another task, branch, worktree, or repository set.

expected.invariant: An unrelated binding is rejected and never enters the same-task epoch-supersession path.

cases.scenario: A required observer remains empty after every meaningful safe fallback, and proving the claim now requires a different observer or narrower claim authority.

expected.invariant: Incomplete is not a fifth route; the verifier names the smallest observer or claim decision needed.
